newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada July housing starts rise 2.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada July housing starts rise 2.7 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts rose by 2.7 percent in July to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 144,700 units from a revised 140,900 units in June, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Monday.
Actual housing starts fell to 14,822 in July from a revised 15,031 the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said the increase in construction of multiple units accounted for most of July's performance.

"Low mortgage rates, faster job creation and improving consumer confidence continue to have a positive impact on single-detached construction," Louis Trottier, an economist at CMHC, said in a statement.
The provincial estimates are for centers with more than 10,000 people. The other area estimates are for centers with less than 10,000.
